title: Relations and Functions: Cartesian Products, Domain and Range
seo_title: Relations and Functions Class 11 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 2)
standard_text: Ordered pairs, Cartesian product of sets, number of elements in the Cartesian product of two finite sets; definition of relation, pictorial diagrams, domain, co-domain and range of a relation; function as a special type of relation; domain, co-domain and range of a function; real valued functions and their graphs: constant, identity, polynomial, rational, modulus, signum and greatest integer functions; sum, difference, product and quotients of functions (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 11 Relations and Functions worksheet (NCERT Chapter 2): Cartesian products, number of relations, domain and range, functions, modulus, signum and greatest integer functions, and algebra of functions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A function gives each element of the domain exactly one image.
key_sub: n(A × B) = n(A) × n(B); there are 2^(mn) relations from A to B.
body_html:
How it works

  • A × B = {(a, b) : a ∈ A, b ∈ B}. If n(A) = m and n(B) = n, then n(A × B) = mn.
  • A relation from A to B is any subset of A × B, so there are 2mn of them.
  • The domain is the set of first elements, the range the set of second elements.
  • A relation is a function when every element of the domain has exactly one image.
  • Special functions: |x| (modulus), signum (1, 0 or −1) and [x] (greatest integer ≤ x).
Example

A = {1, 2}, B = {3, 4, 5}. How many relations are there from A to B?

n(A × B) = 2 × 3 = 6

2⁶ = 64

Answer: 64

Common mistakes

  • Using n(A) + n(B) for n(A × B).
  • Swapping domain and range.
  • Thinking [−2.5] = −2 (it is −3).
